evals.prompt:
Evaluate four proposed ML projects and tell us candidly which ones should **skip SageMaker** in favor of simpler managed AWS services versus which genuinely belong on SageMaker:
1. Zero-shot contract Q&A + RAG over 50,000 PDFs with PII redaction.
2. Extracting key-value fields and tables from scanned invoices.
3. A `1.2 GB` scikit-learn Docker container invoked 80 times/day (`< 3s` CPU runtime).
4. Custom PyTorch multi-label defect segmentation on proprietary factory camera imagery (`500K` labeled masks, `< 40 ms` edge/cloud GPU SLA).
evals.expected_output: Applies the Phase 2 'Skip SageMaker?' gate honestly: (1) -> **Amazon Bedrock** (`Converse` + Knowledge Bases + Guardrails, zero GPU ops); (2) -> **Amazon Textract** (managed OCR/forms/tables); (3) -> **AWS Lambda (Container Image `<= 10 GB`)** or **SageMaker Serverless Inference**; (4) -> **Amazon SageMaker AI** (Tier C Managed Training Job with Managed Spot + Real-Time GPU/`ml.inf2` hosting).
expectations: Activates the sagemaker-solution-architect skill

Recommends **skipping SageMaker** for Workloads 1, 2, and 3: routing (1) to **Amazon Bedrock** (Knowledge Bases + Guardrails), (2) to **Amazon Textract**, and (3) to **AWS Lambda Container** (or SageMaker Serverless Inference)
Selects **Amazon SageMaker AI** (Tier C Managed Training + GPU/`inf2` inference) for Workload 4 (proprietary computer-vision segmentation)

evals.prompt:
Map four training workloads to the exact Training Tier (Tier A, Tier B, Tier C, or Tier D) and explain how `ap-south-1` regional availability changes Tier B:
1. Business analysts forecasting weekly SKU sales with Indian holiday calendars and zero custom PyTorch code.
2. LoRA `RLVRTrainer` fine-tuning of Qwen-2.5-7B in `us-west-2` vs in `ap-south-1`.
3. Custom multi-GPU PyTorch FSDP fine-tuning of a vision-language model on 4 `ml.g6e.12xlarge` nodes with Spot checkpointing.
4. Multi-week frontier pre-training across `128 × ml.p5.48xlarge` nodes requiring 3200 Gbps EFAv2, FSx for Lustre, and automatic faulty-GPU node replacement.
evals.expected_output: Maps (1) to **Tier A — Autopilot AutoMLv2** (`CreateAutoMLJobV2` with `HolidayConfig` -> `sagemaker-training-architect`); (2) to **Tier B — Serverless FM Customization** (`finetuning`) in `us-west-2`, **AND notes Tier B is unsupported in `ap-south-1`**, routing `ap-south-1` LoRA training to **Tier C** (`sagemaker-training-architect`); (3) to **Tier C — Managed Training Jobs** (`@remote`/Estimators + Spot + FastFile -> `sagemaker-training-architect`); and (4) to **Tier D — SageMaker HyperPod** (EKS/Slurm + EFAv2 + FSx for Lustre + auto node-healing).
expectations: Activates the sagemaker-solution-architect skill

Maps Workload 1 to **Tier A (`CreateAutoMLJobV2`)**, Workload 3 to **Tier C (Managed Training Jobs)**, and Workload 4 to **Tier D (SageMaker HyperPod** with EFAv2 + FSx for Lustre + auto node-healing)
Maps Workload 2 to **Tier B (Serverless FM Customization)** in `us-west-2` while explicitly catching that `ap-south-1` lacks Tier B and must route to **Tier C** (`sagemaker-training-architect`)

evals.prompt: Compare `ml.g5`, `ml.g6`, `ml.g6e`, `ml.p4d.24xlarge`, `ml.p5.48xlarge`, `ml.trn1`/`trn2`, and `ml.inf2` on per-chip VRAM/HBM and network bandwidth, and explain why `ml.g6e` (`L40S`) is a sweet spot for hosting 30B–70B models without jumping all the way to `ml.p4d`/`ml.p5`.
evals.expected_output: Contrasts the accelerator families accurately: `ml.g5` (A10G `24 GB`/GPU) & `ml.g6` (L4 `24 GB`/GPU, up to `192 GB` across 8 GPUs), **`ml.g6e` (NVIDIA L40S `48 GB`/GPU — 2× VRAM per GPU vs `g5`/`g6`, up to `384 GB` on `g6e.48xl` + up to 400 Gbps EFA, fitting 30B–70B models cleanly without `p4d`)**, `ml.p4d`/`p4de` (8× A100 `40/80 GB` = `320/640 GB`, 400 Gbps EFA), `ml.p5`/`p5e` (8× H100/H200 `80/141 GB` = `640 GB / 1.1 TB`, 3200 Gbps EFAv2), `ml.trn1`/`trn2` (`32/96 GB` HBM/chip, ~50% lower training cost), and `ml.inf2` (`32 GB` HBM/chip, 2 NeuronCores/chip, ~35–50% lower `$/token`).
expectations: Activates the sagemaker-solution-architect skill
Contrasts `ml.g5`/`ml.g6` (`24 GB`/GPU) with **`ml.g6e` (`48 GB` L40S/GPU, up to `384 GB` total + EFA)**, explaining why `ml.g6e` hosts 30B–70B models without requiring `ml.p4d`/`ml.p5`
Accurately summarizes `ml.p4d` (A100 `320/640 GB`), `ml.p5` (H100 `640 GB` / 3200 Gbps EFAv2), `ml.trn1`/`trn2` (Trainium training), and `ml.inf2` (Inferentia2 `32 GB`/chip, 2 NeuronCores)

evals.prompt: Our solution review board needs a crisp decision table contrasting payload limits, timeout limits, and ideal scale across (1) Real-Time `InferenceComponent` Bin-Packing, (2) Serverless Inference, (3) Asynchronous Inference, (4) Multi-Model Endpoint (MME), and (5) Batch Transform.
evals.expected_output: Contrasts exact limits: (1) Real-Time `InferenceComponent` (`<= 6 MB` payload, `60s` timeout, fractional/multi-GPU bin-packing + `MinCapacity=0` for 2–50 distinct models); (2) Serverless Inference (`<= 4 MB` payload, `60s` timeout, `1–6 GB` CPU RAM only, `<= 200` concurrency); (3) Asynchronous Inference (**up to `1 GB` payload**, **up to `1-hour` timeout**, S3 queues + `MinCapacity=0`); (4) MME (`<= 6 MB` payload, `60s` timeout, 100s–1,000s of homogeneous models dynamically cached from S3); (5) Batch Transform (offline S3 dataset scoring, hours/days, `$0` standing cost).
expectations: Activates the sagemaker-solution-architect skill

States accurate payload and timeout ceilings across Real-Time `InferenceComponent` (`<= 6 MB`, `60s`), Serverless (`<= 4 MB`, `60s`, `1–6 GB` CPU), and Asynchronous Inference (**up to `1 GB`**, **up to `1 hour`**)

Distinguishes `InferenceComponent` bin-packing (heterogeneous GPU/CPU models with isolated copies) from MME (100s–1,000s of homogeneous models sharing one container) and Batch Transform (offline S3 jobs)

Addresses Well-Architected ML Lens controls (`VpcOnly` + KMS CMK + 5-persona IAM, Iceberg Feature Store + MLflow lineage reproducibility, and multi-AZ Blue/Green rollback)

evals.prompt: How do you choose the right training data storage & I/O mode on SageMaker between S3 `File` mode, S3 `FastFile` mode (`ShardedByS3Key`), WebDataset `.tar` sharding, and Amazon FSx for Lustre when GPUs sit at 18% utilization starving on `5 million` tiny 15 KB JPEG images?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses small-file metadata I/O starvation: S3 `File` mode copies all 5M tiny objects upfront (massive startup delay), and unsharded `FastFile` suffers per-file HTTP/POSIX open overhead on millions of tiny files; prescribes packing tiny JPEGs into **WebDataset `.tar` shards** (`100–500 MB` per shard) streamed via `FastFile` + `ShardedByS3Key`, OR mounting **Amazon FSx for Lustre** (or S3 Express One Zone) for sub-millisecond POSIX random-access I/O across multi-node clusters.
expectations: Activates the sagemaker-solution-architect skill
Diagnoses GPU I/O starvation caused by millions of tiny `15 KB` S3 objects under `File` / unsharded access
Recommends **WebDataset `.tar` sharding** with `FastFile` (`ShardedByS3Key`) and/or **Amazon FSx for Lustre** (or S3 Express One Zone) for high-throughput multi-GPU/multi-node training
